subject: Security questionnaire: PII classification, access controls & dataflow — NovaHealth
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@novahealth.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.com
Cc: dpo@novahealth.com
Date: 2026-06-01T08:15:00+02:00
Subject: Security questionnaire: PII classification, access controls & dataflow — NovaHealth

Hi Connor,

Thanks for the demo last week — NovaHealth's Security & Privacy team has a short set of follow-ups to close our DPA review. We're trying to map exactly how PII flows from our integration point through your stack and what subprocessors touch unredacted identifiers. Could you help with the following?

1) Data classification: list the categories of PII Redwood stores or processes when handling our calls (examples: user identifiers, health-related free-text, metadata, device IDs).

2) Access controls: which internal roles can view raw PII (not pseudonymized)? Please list role names and whether access is logged/audited.

3) Dataflow diagram: we need a current diagram showing ingress point (NovaHealth API), transient storage, batch exports (if any), and any cross-border paths. A PDF is ideal.

4) Subprocessors: we need an exportable roster (company name, purpose, country, Data Processing Agreement link).

5) Retention & deletion: default retention for request logs, cached KV entries, and embeddings derived from PII. Also explain deletion workflow when a customer requests data erasure.

Given our timelines, a short written response + artifacts by EOD Tuesday (2026-06-02) would help our legal/ops signoff. If any items require a redline to the DPA, flag them and we'll route to procurement.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Rossi
Head of Security Operations — NovaHealth
elena.rossi@novahealth.com

From: connor_obrien@redwood.com
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@novahealth.com>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-01T09:30:00+02:00
Subject: Re: Security questionnaire: PII classification, access controls & dataflow — NovaHealth

Elena,

Appreciate the clear list — answered inline below and attaching artifacts: data_flow_v2.pdf (diagram), subprocessors_inventory_20260601.csv (exportable roster), and the latest DPA (DPA_NovaHealth_v3.docx) with a couple of marginal notes.

1) Data classification
- User identifiers: account_id, email, phone — stored in encrypted metadata for routing.
- Application content: free-text prompts/responses — by default kept transiently in runtime memory and token cache; persisted only when customers enable logs or retainments.
- Health-related content: treated as Sensitive Personal Data (SPD) in our classification — flagged and handled with stricter retention.
- Device & network metadata: IPs (hashed at rest), user-agent strings (stored as non-identifying metadata unless used for debugging).

2) Access controls
- Roles with access to unredacted PII (examples):
  * SRE (incident triage): can access raw logs via just-in-time (JIT) privileged sessions — access requires two-person approval and is logged.
  * Customer Support Engineers: access to redacted logs by default; can escalate to view unredacted material only with manager approval and a written justification.
  * Security Team / DPOs: full access for investigations with audit trail.
- All accesses generate entries in our audit log (immutable) and are retained for 18 months by default. Logs include user, reason, and duration.

3) Dataflow diagram
- See attached data_flow_v2.pdf for the flow from NovaHealth API -> Redwood edge -> inference runtime -> caching layer -> optional export (S3) or push to customer's VPC. The PDF includes callouts for transient KV cache behavior and where encryption applies.

4) Subprocessors
- Attached CSV lists current subprocessors, purpose, and country. Notable ones:
  * Cloud object storage: NimbusStorage Inc. (US) — logs & artifacts (encrypted).
  * Observability: TraceSight Ltd. (IE) — telemetry (pseudonymized by default).
  * Key management: KeyVaultCo (DE) — optional KMS integration for customer-managed keys.
- We run quarterly reviews and provide a notification window for onshore-only carve-outs.

5) Retention & deletion
- Request logs: default retention 90 days.
- KV cache: TTL varies by config; default 0 (no persistence) for hosted customers, configurable for dedicated/private.
- Embeddings derived from PII: by default not persisted unless the customer opts in; when persisted, retention defaults to 365 days.
- Deletion workflow: customer issues a deletion request via console or support ticket -> automation searches indexed stores and marks objects for deletion -> background job securely wipes S3 keys and updates manifest. We provide a deletion certificate for audits.

Next steps / asks from us:
- Please confirm whether NovaHealth will enable log retention or embeddings persistence.
- If you need onshore-only subprocessors, call that out and we can map options (some subprocessors have EU-hosted alternatives).

Attachment stubs:
- data_flow_v2.pdf (diagram, 1.4MB)
- subprocessors_inventory_20260601.csv (CSV, 34KB)
- DPA_NovaHealth_v3.docx (editable DPA)

Connor O'Brien

connor_obrien@redwood.com

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@novahealth.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.com

Date: 2026-06-02T09:10:00+02:00
Subject: Re: Security questionnaire: PII classification, access controls & dataflow — NovaHealth

Connor — thanks for the quick turnaround and artifacts. A couple of clarifying items before we finalize: 

- For SRE and Security JIT access: can you confirm whether sessions are time-limited and whether session recordings (screens) are captured? We need to document session scope for our auditors.
- On embeddings: if we opt in to embeddings persistence, can we request per-account encryption keys (bring-your-own-key)?
- Subprocessors CSV: I see TraceSight in Ireland — does TraceSight receive any unredacted PII? The CSV lists "telemetry" only but we need to be explicit.
- Cross-border: the diagram shows an option to route inference through a US region if EU capacity is constrained. Can Redwood commit to EU-only routing for NovaHealth (contractual) and provide an SLA/penalty if that routing is not honored?

Procurement also flagged the DPA margins; they asked whether Redwood can accept a clause that subprocessors must be approved for EU-only processing when required.

We aim to close this by EOD Thursday. If you prefer, we can set a 30-minute call to resolve the remaining items.

Best,
Elena

From: connor_obrien@redwood.com
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@novahealth.com>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-02T14:04:00+02:00
Subject: Re: Security questionnaire: PII classification, access controls & dataflow — NovaHealth

Elena — appreciate the thorough review. Answers below and a proposed path to close fast:

- SRE / JIT sessions: sessions are time-limited (default 30 minutes) and require two approvers for escalation. We capture command-level audit logs and a full access record (user, timestamp, reason). We do not capture screen recordings by default; if NovaHealth requires session recordings for high-sensitivity investigations, we can enable them under a tailored access policy and document retention.

- Embeddings & BYOK: yes — for Dedicated and Private customers we support customer-managed keys (KMS) so embeddings at rest can be encrypted with customer keys. Hosted customers can opt into our managed KM offering; BYOK requires an enterprise addendum which is included in the DPA_NovaHealth_v3.docx (see section 8).

- TraceSight (IE): they process pseudonymized telemetry only. No long-term access to unredacted PII. Their access is limited to telemetry aggregates and hashed identifiers for sampling. We'll add an explicit note to the CSV and produce an annex stating "no unredacted PII transmitted to TraceSight."

- EU-only routing: we can commit to EU-only routing for NovaHealth. Operationally that means:
  * Model routing policy pinned to EU regions for all requests from your account.
  * Fallback to non-EU targets only on explicit written approval or prolonged outage (>5m) with notification.
  * We'll add a contractual clause with an SLA credit for violations. Draft language is in the DPA margins (proposed clause: Section 12.4.a - Data Residency Commitment).

Procurement ask on subprocessor approvals: we can add a process where NovaHealth gets a 30-day notification window for new subprocessors and an approval path for EU-only processing carve-outs. We'll add proposed text to the DPA and can accept a limited approval right for EU-only subprocessors in scope.

Proposed next steps:
1) I'll update the CSV to add the TraceSight text and re-send.
2) Markus (cc'd) will prepare the contractual phrasing for the EU-routing SLA and the subprocessor approval process.
3) If it helps, let's schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow; happy to loop Legal/Procurement.

Attachment stubs included again: data_flow_v2.pdf, subprocessors_inventory_20260601.csv, DPA_NovaHealth_v3.docx

Connor
